questions.question: A can finish a piece of work in a certain number of days. B takes 45% more number of days to finish the same work independently. They worked together for 58 days and then the remaining work was done by B alone in 29 days. In how many days could A have completed the work, had he worked alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

B takes 45% more number of days to finish the same work independently.

They worked together for 58 days and then the remaining work was done by B alone in 29 days.

**Formula:**

Total work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Let number of days taken by A to complete the work be 100 days

Number of days taken by B to complete the work = 100 × (1
45/100) = 145

Time ratio of A to that of B = 100 : 145 = 20 : 29

Efficiency ratio of A to that of B = 29 : 20

Let efficiency of A = 29 unit/day

Efficiency of B = 20 unit/day

Work done by A and B in 58 days = (29 + 20) × 58 = 49 × 58 = 2842 unit

Remaining work which is done by B in 29 days = 20 × 29 = 580 unit

Total work = 2842 + 580 = 3422 unit

∴ Time taken by A to complete the whole work = 3422/29 = 118

questions.question: P does half as much work as Q in 1/3 of the time. If together they take 15 days to complete a work, how many days will P take to do it alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let Q completed the work in x days

P completed the 1/2 of the work = x/3

⇒ P completed the whole work = 2x/3

**Formula used:**

Total work = Efficiency × time

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

1/(2x/3) + 1/(x) = 1/15

⇒ 3/2x + 1/x = 1/15

⇒ 5/2x = 1/15

⇒ x = 5 × 15/2

**∴ P completed the whole work alone = 2x/3 = 2/3 × 5 × 15/2 = 25 days**

questions.question: S does half as much work as T in 1/7 of the time taken by T. If together they take 21 days to complete a work, then how many days shall S take to complete that work alone?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Total work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Let S and T take ‘x’ and ‘y’ days respectively to do the work alone

S’s 1 day work = 1/x

T’s 1 day work = 1/y

Now, S does half as much work as T in 1/7 of the time taken by T

⇒ S’s 1 day work = 1/2 × T’s 7 days work

⇒ 1/x = 1/2 × 7/y

⇒ 1/y = 2/7x ----(1)

Together they complete the work in 21 days,

⇒ S’s 1 day work + T’s 1 day work = 1/21

⇒ 1/x + 1/y = 1/21

Substituting from (1),

⇒ 1/x + 2/7x = 1/21

⇒ 9/7x = 1/21

⇒ x = 21 × 9/7 = 27

**∴ S will take 27 days to do the work alone**

questions.question: A can complete a certain work in 30 days. He started the work. After 4 days, B joined him and the whole work was completed in 10 days from the beginning. B alone can complete one-third of the same work in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 30 days

Time taken by B to complete the work after 4 days = 10 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Let B can complete the work in x days

Time taken by A to complete the work in 1 day = 1/30 units

Time taken by B to complete the work in 1 day = 1/x units

According to the question

⇒ 10 × 1/30 + (10 – 4) × 1/x = 1

⇒ 1/3 + 6/x = 1

⇒ 6/x = (1 – 1/3)

⇒ 6/x = 2/3

⇒ 2x = 18

⇒ x = 9

B alone can complete one-third of the same work = (1/3 × 9)

⇒ 3 days

**∴ The required time is 3 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

According to the question, A can complete a work in 30 days, 

After 4 days of work B join and completed the remaining work next 6 days, 

What A alone can do in 26 days that work A + B can do in 6 days, so

⇒ A × 26 = (A + B) × 6

⇒ 26A = 6A + 6B

⇒ A/B = 6/20 = 3/10

So, total work is 30 × 3 = 90 unit

Now, B can do 1/3ᵣd of the work in 90 × 1/3 × 1/10 = 3 days

questions.question: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 15 days. B and C together can do it in 24 days. If A is twice as good a workman as C, then in how many days can B alone complete the work ?
questions.solution:
**Given **

A and B together can complete work = 15 days 

B and C together can complete work = 24 days 

**Formula Used **

Work = time × efficiency 

**Calculation **

Take LCM of (15, 24) = 120 

Let the total work be 120 

Efficiency of A and B = 120/15 = 8 ----(1)

Efficiency of B and C = 120/24 = 5 ----(2)

We know , A : C = 2 : 1 ----(3) 

From (1) and (2) 

⇒ A - C = 3 

By using (3) , efficiency of A = 6 , B = 2 and C = 3

⇒ B alone can complete the work in days = 120/2 = 60 days 

**∴ B alone can complete the work in days is 60 days **

questions.question: P, Q and R can complete a work alone in 12,15 and 20 days respectively. They started the work together. P left the work 8 days before the work was completed and Q left the work 5 days after P had left. R completed the remaining work alone. How many days will be required to complete the whole work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P can complete the work in 12 days.

Q can complete the work in 15 days.

R can complete the work in 20 days.

P left the work 8 days before it was completed.

Q left the work 5 days after P had left.

R completed the remaining work alone.

**Concept:**

The total work done by individuals working together is equal to the sum of their individual work done in the same time.

**Solution:**

Total work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60

Efficiency of P = 60/12 = 5

Efficiency of Q = 60/15 = 4

Efficiency of R = 60/20 = 3

Let the total work done in t days.

According to question,

⇒ 5(t - 8) + 4(t - 3) + 3t = 60

⇒ 5t - 40 + 4t - 12 + 3t = 60

⇒ 12t = 112

⇒ t = 112/12 = 28/3 days

**∴ 28/3 days will be required to complete the whole work.**
